scenario.name: kong-cost-caps
scenario.description: Test 3 on Kong OSS 3.9.3, run through run-cost.sh with a throwaway consumer (its limit in the run's meta.json note). No rate limit. Per-request caps: each case asks for a long answer and up to 2000 tokens. Gemini's cap comes from kong.yaml (model.options.max_tokens 256), which overrides the caller's max_tokens (llm/drivers/shared.lua merge_config_defaults) and replaces the dropped max_completion_tokens; Claude's native request passes through with the caller's max_tokens. The Claude case replaces the harness's two-sentence system instruction so its answer can run past 256 tokens; the Gemini cases keep it, and are cut short anyway by default-level thinking inside the 256 cap. Kong's log (kong-log.json) shows what it counted and priced: Gemini's usage and cost, nothing for Claude (preserve route, log_statistics off).
